title: ArreSTick motif controls beta-arrestin-binding stability and extends phosphorylation-dependent beta-arrestin interactions to non-receptor proteins.
authors: Toth, Andras David; Soltesz-Katona, Eszter; Kis, Katalin; Guti, Viktor; Gilzer, Sharon; Prokop, Susanne; Boros, Roxana; Misak, Adam; Balla, Andras; Varnai, Peter; Turiak, Lilla; Acs, Andras; Drahos, Laszlo; Inoue, Asuka; Hunyady, Laszlo; Turu, Gabor
one_liner_zh: 该文用1D序列卷积模型识别β-arrestin结合所需的磷酸化基序arreSTick，并发现其存在于非受体蛋白（含转录因子HTATSF1）中，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作与序列模型，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无三维结合建模或TF-DNA机制研究，仅边缘相关。
abstract: The binding and function of beta-arrestins are regulated by specific phosphorylation motifs present in G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). However, the exact arrangement of phosphorylated amino acids responsible for establishing a stable interaction remains unclear. We employ a 1D sequence convolution model trained on GPCRs with established beta-arrestin-binding properties. With this approach, amino acid motifs characteristic of GPCRs that form stable interactions with beta-arrestins can be identified, a pattern that we name "arreSTick." Intriguingly, the arreSTick pattern is also present in numerous non-receptor proteins. Using proximity biotinylation assay and mass spectrometry analysis, we demonstrate that the arreSTick motif controls the interaction between many non-receptor proteins and beta-arrestin2. The HIV-1 Tat-specific factor 1 (HTSF1 or HTATSF1), a nuclear transcription factor, contains the arreSTick pattern, and its subcellular localization is influenced by beta-arrestin2. Our findings unveil a broader role for beta-arrestins in phosphorylation-dependent interactions, extending beyond GPCRs to encompass non-receptor proteins as well.
abstract_zh: β-arrestins的结合与功能受G蛋白偶联受体（GPCRs）中特定磷酸化基序的调控。然而，负责建立稳定相互作用的磷酸化氨基酸的确切排列仍不清楚。我们采用一个在具有已确立β-arrestin结合特性的GPCRs上训练的1D序列卷积模型。通过这种方法，可以识别出与β-arrestins形成稳定相互作用的GPCRs特征性氨基酸基序，我们将这一模式命名为“arreSTick”。有趣的是，arreSTick模式也存在于众多非受体蛋白中。利用邻近生物素化测定和质谱分析，我们证明arreSTick基序控制许多非受体蛋白与β-arrestin2之间的相互作用。HIV-1 Tat特异性因子1（HTSF1或HTATSF1），一种核转录因子，含有arreSTick模式，其亚细胞定位受β-arrestin2影响。我们的发现揭示了β-arrestins在磷酸化依赖性相互作用中的更广泛作用，其范围从GPCRs扩展到非受体蛋白。
